criterion: 4 — a ChatGPT terminal is opened from the dashboard and its greet is seen on the page (Playwright screenshot), not inferred from a stub
section: Phase 4 — live Playwright sign-off and v1.2.12 ship gate
message: The only operator proof is skippable (`ANCHOR_TESTS_ALLOW_LIVE=1`) and the ship rule is "the screenshot file exists." No greet string is named. A blank xterm, a Codex login wall, an approval modal, or a copied PNG all satisfy "file exists." Criterion 4 is a claim about John's page, not about a path on disk. As written, v1.2.12 can ship with the greet still inferred.

criterion: 1 — the lane seed is written exactly once and the greet arrives
section: Phase 4 — live sign-off test / Phase 2 seed timing
message: The dashboard action the live test clicks is "Open terminal," which is a bare `general` session — historically no lane skill. Playwright then waits for unnamed "Codex greet text" and records `seed_delivery`, which is not the skill loading. Criterion 1 is a seeded trio cockpit, not a chrome banner. An operator who then starts Research/Plan/Build on ChatGPT is running the unproven path. Phase 2's stub done-when (`seeded True`) and Phase 4's live button do not even agree on which lane is the proof.

criterion: 2 — picker shows "ChatGPT — ready"; a host without the Codex binary still fails closed; risk table — picker shows "unavailable" there
message: Phase 1 sets `selectable=True`, `status='ready'`, and a static reason "Codex CLI detected…" with no detection. Tests pin "no seat is disabled." On a host without `codex`, the operator is told the seat is ready and detected, then `term_start` dies with `chatgpt-terminal-binary-missing`. The North Star already chose the operator-visible mitigation — the picker says unavailable — and this draft implements the opposite lie.

criterion: 2 — the Terminal picker shows "ChatGPT — ready" AND 1 — PTY running the Codex TUI with `--cd`, `--no-alt-screen`, `-s workspace-write`
section: Phase 1 done-when vs Phase 2 launch argv
message: Phase 1's definition of done is the picker and capability note saying ready, while the launch is still bare `codex` (alt-screen, no `--cd`, no sandbox). That is the operator-visible surface going green before the terminal can actually open as specified. Any mid-effort restart, or a saved `default_cli=chatgpt` after wave 1, presents a first-class seat that hits the exact alt-screen failure the risk table named. "Ready" is a surface claim, not a permission to open a gate.

criterion: 1 — `POST /api/rnd/term_set_engine` switches a live session to and from ChatGPT; the lane seed is written exactly once and the greet arrives
section: Phase 2 — seed timing / switch_engine relaunch sites
message: First-output-gated seed is specified for `start_session`. Engine switch is the operator's other way onto ChatGPT (criterion 1 names it). The draft applies launch argv at both relaunch sites but does not apply `SEED_AFTER_FIRST_OUTPUT_BACKENDS` there. Toggling Claude → ChatGPT can dump the skill into a composer that is not up — the seed-before-ready risk, on the hotter operator path. Phase 4 asserts no orphan PTY after toggle, not that the ChatGPT side was seeded after first output.

criterion: 1 — approvals left to the user in the terminal; risk table — seed must not land before the TUI is ready, nor as an approval
message: On timeout the plan still writes the seed ("never leave a live session silently unseeded"). That is how a login wall or on-request approval becomes the seed's target — the operator's first keystrokes answer Codex, or the skill is submitted as the approval. The draft also refuses to inject `-a` and treats "no flag" as "on-request," which is an assumption about v0.151 defaults, not a pin. Criterion 1's approval contract is therefore unenforced on the path most likely to fire on a real open.

criterion: 3 — session usage state is `uncorrelated`; any rollup that includes it is stamped `partial (chatgpt segment unmeasured)` — never an mtime guess, never a fabricated $0.00
message: The draft asserts three stamps at once: empty `stored_engine_uuid` → W4 `uncorrelated`; `usage_unmeasured_segments` + `classify_session_usage` "measured + any segment → STATE_PARTIAL"; and "ended on chatgpt with no reason is stamped chatgpt-segment." The operator-facing badge is then whichever branch wins. Criterion 3 split session vs rollup on purpose. As written, a ChatGPT session can show as partial, or a rollup can inherit a session-level reason, and the "no $0.00 / never mtime" test does not say which widget John reads.

The function is stub-tested. The done-when then names "the Doctor Diagnose button with backend chatgpt" without saying how that button chooses ChatGPT — default_cli, a picker, or a hidden argument. John does not call `live_doctor_session`. If Diagnose stays on Claude (or on write-posture default_cli), the read-only Codex Doctor never appears on the surface criterion 3 is for. A stub argv walk is not Doctor-capable in the cockpit.

criterion: Doctor posture and honest accounting — session usage state is uncorrelated and any rollup that includes it is stamped partial (chatgpt segment unmeasured); never an mtime guess, never a fabricated $0.00
section: Phase 3 — Doctor read-only posture and honest unmeasured accounting
message: Criterion 3 requires two stamps at once: the ChatGPT session is `uncorrelated` (no session-id pin) and a rollup that includes it is `partial (chatgpt segment unmeasured)`. The plan asserts both as done-whens, then specifies a classifier that cannot produce them together: `classify_session_usage` is `measured + any segment → STATE_PARTIAL`, while a chatgpt-START session is `stored_engine_uuid == ''` so the W4 finalize path yields `uncorrelated`. Those are different states. A session that is not `measured` never enters the `measured + segment` arm, so the dashboard badge the same phase promises (`partial` / `chatgpt segment unmeasured`) does not fire. The remaining rule — “ended on chatgpt with no reason is stamped chatgpt-segment” — would overwrite `uncorrelated` with `partial` to make the badge green. Either the session stamp is a lie, or the rollup stamp is silent. That is exactly the hole Option C was ruled to close: a builder who needs a green badge will enter the mtime/cwd-window path or write `$0.00` to look measured. The plan names `UNMEASURED_SEGMENT_BACKENDS` and a test that “no cost number is written,” but it never identifies which function emits which stamp, nor what `classify_session_usage` returns for an uncorrelated chatgpt-only project. Until that state machine is one table with one test per stamp, criterion 3 is not implementable without fabricating a number or dropping the partial marker.

criterion: A terminal opens on ChatGPT — the lane seed is written exactly once and the greet arrives; before v1.2.12 ships a ChatGPT terminal is opened from the dashboard and its greet is seen on the page (Playwright screenshot), not inferred from a stub
message: The only non-stub proof waits for “the Codex greet text on the page,” does not pin the string, and treats a screenshot file plus `seed_delivery` recorded as the ship gate. Criterion 1’s greet is the lane-skill greet after the seed, not TUI chrome (“OpenAI Codex”, a spinner, a login widget). Those are different dependent variables. A shot of Codex chrome can exist while the seed was dropped, eaten by an approval prompt, or never written — and `seed_delivery='stdin-timeout-fallback'` records the attempt, not arrival. The ship rule is “tag after the PNG exists,” which is a file-presence check, not a pixel check that the seeded greet is on the page. Stub Phase 2 already sets `seeded=True` after `_pty.write` with a stub that emits immediately, so CI cannot falsify this. As written, v1.2.12 can ship on the wrong greet.

criterion: The truth tables agree — Terminal picker shows ChatGPT — ready; a host without the Codex binary still fails closed with chatgpt-terminal-binary-missing; risk table: the picker shows unavailable there
section: Phase 1 — Open the gate and make the truth tables agree
message: Phase 1 hardcodes `selectable=True`, `status='ready'`, reason `'Codex CLI detected; the interactive terminal opens on the Codex TUI…'`. There is no `shutil.which` / resolver probe in that branch. “Detected” is copy, not a measurement. Criterion 2’s happy path (show ready) is therefore true even on a host with no `codex`, while the North Star’s own risk row required the picker to show **unavailable** and leave fail-closed to `chatgpt-terminal-binary-missing`. The plan implements only the resolver raise (and a test that the raise happens before a worktree). The user-visible truth table still says ready. A settings save of `default_cli=chatgpt` on that host then persists a lie that criterion 2 claimed the picker would not tell.

criterion: A terminal opens on ChatGPT — lane seed written exactly once and the greet arrives; approvals left to the user in the terminal; risk table: seed lands before the TUI is ready, or Codex asks for approval on the seed — write after first output; approvals stay on-request
section: Phase 2 — Interactive launch argv and first-output seed
message: The plan operationalizes “TUI ready” as “first PTY byte, else 8s timeout then write anyway.” First output from Codex is not the composer; it is often banner, login, trust, or an approval widget. Writing the lane-skill seed into that widget is the failure mode the risk row named, and the timeout-fallback reintroduces seed-before-ready by design (“never leave unseeded”). The stub PTY “emits output immediately so tests stay fast,” which confounds the test: Phase 2’s `seeded=True` / seed-once walk cannot fail this race. The other half of the same risk row — approvals stay `on-request` — is implemented by **not** passing `-a`. Omission is not a pin; if v0.151’s default is not `on-request`, the seed is auto-answered or auto-blocked and criterion 1’s “approvals left to the user” is false. The positional-argv fallback that would actually own the first turn is deferred until the live run already failed. That is not a mitigation; it is hoping the unmeasured live path is kind.

criterion: With default_cli=chatgpt (or the engine toggle), POST /api/rnd/term_start starts a PTY running the Codex TUI
message: Criterion 1’s treatment is `default_cli=chatgpt` **or** the engine toggle driving `POST /api/rnd/term_start`. The plan proves persistence (`save_settings` / `get_default_cli`) and proves `start_session(..., backend='chatgpt')` when the backend is passed in. It never names the code that reads `get_default_cli()` (or the picker) inside `term_start` / the dashboard “Open terminal” button. Those are different independent variables. If Open terminal still uses `last_engine_for_project` or a hardcoded engine, Phase 1 can persist chatgpt and Phase 4 can set the setting, then click a button that starts Claude and wait for a Codex greet that will not come — or worse, a leftover Codex-chrome flake from another test. “Why now” claimed only the allow-guard plus tables were closed; that is an assumption, not a traced call. Without a named consumer (`term_start` body, JS `newTermSession`, etc.) in a done-when, Foreman will not add the wiring, and the criterion’s actual trigger stays untested except as an implied Playwright hope.

criterion: live_doctor_session(backend="chatgpt") launches with -s read-only (a DOCTOR_READONLY_CLI_ARGS entry)
message: The argv contract (`exactly one -s read-only`, `--cd` = Doctor cwd, `--no-alt-screen`) is specified for a **fresh** stub start. The reuse contract is not: “a second start attaches via `live_doctor_session(mode, backend='chatgpt', posture)` keyed reuse.” If the live key is still `mode` (and maybe `posture`) without `backend`, Diagnose with ChatGPT attaches to an already-open Claude/Grok Doctor and never launches Codex, so the read-only table entry never appears on a PTY. Criterion 3 is the chatgpt Doctor launch, not “some Doctor is up.” The plan also lets `resolve=True` keep `workspace-write`; that is a second posture on the same session object, which makes a mode-only key even more likely to return the wrong engine with the wrong `-s`. No done-when asserts that a live non-chatgpt Doctor does **not** satisfy a `backend='chatgpt'` request, or that the Diagnose button actually passes `backend`. Stub argv on `start_doctor_session` does not measure `live_doctor_session`.

criterion: A terminal opens on ChatGPT with --cd worktree, --no-alt-screen, -s workspace-write; nothing regresses under ANCHOR_PTY_BACKEND=stub + ANCHOR_ENGINE_CMD
section: Phase 2 — argv order asserted under the stub
message: The Codex TUI contract is the launch argv. CI is defined as `ANCHOR_PTY_BACKEND=stub` + `ANCHOR_ENGINE_CMD`. The plan asserts `[<cmd>, '--no-alt-screen', '-s', 'workspace-write', '--cd', <worktree>]` “under the stub” without saying the assertion reads the pre-replacement argv (the list `_interactive_launch_args` returns) rather than the stub command that actually spawned. If `ANCHOR_ENGINE_CMD` replaces the vector, Phase 2’s new test is green while `ENGINE_LAUNCH_ARGS` never reaches a process, and Claude/Grok “byte-unchanged” pins do not protect the chatgpt branch. Criterion 1 then holds only in the skippable live test. Name the probe point or this is another stub-as-population result.
